title: Smt. Mamta Devi Srivastava v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: Vineet Saran, J. & Attau Rahman Masoodi, J.
headnote: The two-year limitation bar in Section 56(2) of the Electricity Act, 2003 does not apply to the regular current bills of a continuing consumer who is being supplied electricity. Where the consumer's line had been reconnected/re-energised and she thereafter paid nothing for years while continuing to receive supply, a demand for those accrued charges is not a belated demand of the kind barred by s.56(2) (which addresses sums first shown as due after long delay, on pain of disconnection) but non-payment of ongoing bills. Whether bills were in fact sent is a disputed question of fact not decidable in writ jurisdiction, and the consumer has an alternative remedy under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the Court declined to exercise Article 226 jurisdiction in favour of a gross defaulter and dismissed the petition.

holding_units.topic: The s.56(2) two-year bar does not apply to a continuing consumer's regular current bills
holding_units.question: Does the s.56(2) two-year limitation bar the recovery of accrued charges from a consumer who continued to be supplied electricity but did not pay?
holding_units.holding: No. The s.56(2) bar does not apply where it is not a case of a belated demand after disconnection but of non-payment of regular bills by a continuing consumer being supplied electricity; the consumer, having paid nothing since re-energisation while consuming, cannot invoke the 12/24-month bar. Whether bills were sent is a disputed fact not for writ jurisdiction, and the remedy lies under Clause 6.5; the Court declined Article 226 relief to a gross defaulter.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Line reconnected in 2009 (respondents) or 2011 (petitioner); the consumer admittedly paid nothing since re-energisation while continuing to receive supply; demand of Rs. 1,29,558 for bills up to December 2013.

principle_tags.application: The s.56(2) limitation protects against belated first demands, not the ongoing accrued bills of a continuing consumer still being supplied; a gross defaulter who paid nothing while consuming cannot invoke it.
A dispute about whether bills were sent is a disputed fact for the Clause 6.5 remedy, not the writ court.

not_decided.point: Whether regular bills were in fact served on the consumer
not_decided.note: Disputed question of fact not decided in writ jurisdiction; left to the Clause 6.5 remedy.
